items.title: Live: Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US aircraft during rescue effort
items.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) says the American aircraft was "destroyed by the fighters of Islam in the southern region of Isfahan", according to local media reports. Follow live.

items.title: Japan assures Australia will get 'normal supply' of fuel
items.description: Fuel will continue to flow from Japan into Australia under assurances given during recent talks between the two countries.

items.title: 'Painful beyond words': Sisters of Dezi Freeman to sue Victoria Police
items.description: Leading Senior Constable Neal Thompson's sisters plan to launch legal action against Victoria Police over his death. They also say they felt "abandoned" by police after their brother's death.

items.title: As reputation frays, Australia's $54b university brand faces a reckoning
items.description: A generation ago studying in Australia opened doors. Today rising costs and falling satisfaction are making international students think twice, and locals feel sidelined.

items.title: The Kremlin's internet purge is like 'the Soviet era on steroids'
items.description: The Kremlin is increasing its efforts to dictate the narrative in Russia by shutting off the internet, restricting foreign messenger apps and punishing citizens for speaking out.

items.title: Police look for missing cocaine after ocean 'drop-off' during 'bizarre' journey
items.description: Setting off from Panama just before Christmas, police say the MV Raider started its journey towards Sydney with almost 6 tonnes of cocaine aboard worth nearly $2 billion.

items.title: Trash or treasure? Albanese's big gamble
items.description: Labor's landslide re-election brought renewed hope of reform, but in the past 12 months many anti-gambling advocates only became further disillusioned.

items.title: 'Doesn't make any sense': Young Aussies can't justify fuel costs to get to work
items.description: Young people are taking extraordinary steps to deal with the fuel crisis, including cutting back on work because the cost of fuel to get there is now higher than the money they will earn for the shift.

items.title: Australians find joy amid global uncertainty in Easter celebrations
items.description: Christians of all denominations gather at churches and cathedrals to mark Easter and reflect on their faith amid recent global turmoil.

items.title: Live: Rowell returns as unbeaten Suns take on Demons
items.description: Gold Coast and Western Bulldogs look to maintain the last remaining 100 per cent records in the AFL, as they take on the Demons at the MCG and the Bombers at Docklands. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Desperate Raiders head north to face Knights
items.description: With Canberra riding a three-match losing streak the Raiders will be extra keen as they take on the Knights at a sold out stadium in Newcastle. Follow live.

items.title: Queen at 100 is honoured in fashion exhibition as Andrew scandal bites
items.description: Within palace walls the Queen was a godlike figure. As her glorious fashion goes on display to commemorate what would have been her 100th birthday, how would she have responded to the Andrew crisis if alive today?

items.title: Live: Record crowd for gripping conclusion to heated Kings-36ers NBL Finals
items.description: The NBL Finals between the Sydney Kings and Adelaide 36ers come down to game five after a heated series. Follow live.

items.title: Stagflation is already happening, a leading economist warns
items.description: With stagflation risks rising, what lessons could the treasurer learn from the past?

items.title: Changing genders wasn't going to change how I felt about Kate
items.description: Kate could see her husband was miserable as a man and says she couldn't watch Marti be unhappy.

items.title: It hosted Kidman and Luhrmann, now famed regional cinema is up for sale
items.description: It's the cinema good enough for Luhrmann, Jackman and Kidman, and now this North Queensland icon is up for sale after 64 years.

items.title: Lily's grandmother defied 50s' social norms to be both an artist and a mother
items.description: A new show at the Heide Museum of Modern Art explores how the famous Heide Circle reimagined the family in radical ways in the 50s and 60s.

items.title: Whole villages in Sumatra erased overnight — and still living in the wreckage
items.description: Months after floods killed more than a thousand people across Sumatra, residents are still digging their way out of the wreckage. While survivors are eager to rebuild, many just can’t shake the fear that the next catastrophe is just around the corner.

items.title: Man in serious condition after being shot by Tasmania Police
items.description: A man is in a serious but stable condition after being shot by police during an altercation in Hobart's northern suburbs early on Sunday morning.

items.title: Travellers celebrate as major highway reopens after Cyclone Narelle
items.description: Holiday makers took a gamble heading to WA's north hoping a major highway would reopen in time for Easter.

items.title: Artemis crew enter day four with plans to take manual control of spacecraft
items.description: The Artemis astronauts have been taking a moment to look back at Earth as they continue deep into space toward the Moon.

items.title: Walsh facing up to six weeks on sidelines with fractured cheekbone
items.description: The Brisbane Broncos are dealt a massive blow in their NRL premiership defence, with Reece Walsh set for a lengthy stint away from the game.

items.title: Motorists urged to dob in service stations over fuel price hikes
items.description: The NSW government fast-tracks a compliance blitz to strengthen fuel price transparency and protect motorists from misleading pricing.

items.title: After NT spent 'ridiculous' millions on aircraft, operations move offshore
items.description: A modern version of a 1960s-era aircraft that can land on sea and snow was meant to be built in NSW, and then in the NT. But years later it still hasn’t taken off.

items.title: Too young for social media, but old enough to be locked up
items.description: As a nation, we have decided that a teenager cannot navigate a social media algorithm, but a 10-year-old can navigate a courtroom. For Australia's 2025 UN youth representative Satara Uthayakumaran, the contradiction is impossible to ignore.
